official.description_text:
Doctoral student in non-Newtonian fluid mechanics and AI
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences
Project description
Third-cycle subject:
Engineering Mechanics
Within EU doctoral network F
airCFD
, this project will combine high-performance computing, experiments and artificial intelligence in non-Newtonian flows, with the aim of improving rheological characterisation and modelling. In particular, we will design a digital twin rheometer to reliably measure complex fluid parameters in time-varying and chaotic flows.
We will use modern AI techniques to exploit spatial patterns in the computational and experimental data and optimize parameter sensitivity. The researcher will join the dynamic Complex
Fluids Research group
, have access to the supercomputing facilities at KTH, the Swedish e-Science Research Centre (
SeRC
) and the excellent research environment
FLOW
.
Supervision:
Outi Tammisola and Fredrik Lundell are proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission.
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
Mobility rules
- Candidates must not have resided or conducted their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Sweden for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately preceding the recruitment date,
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge.
A suitable background for this position is a master's degree in engineering, mathematics or physics with a focus on fluid mechanics, computational or experimental methods, and/or applied mathematics.
In addition to the above, there is also a
mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach,
analyze and work with complex issues,
strong motivation for doctoral studies, ability to work independently, critical analysis as well as possessing good levels of cooperative and communicative skills.
After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Target degree: Doctoral Degree
Information regarding admission and employment
Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. In the case of studies that are to be completed with a licentiate degree, the total period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for two years.
As a doctoral student, you are entitled to a workplace with
many employee benefits
and monthly salary according to
KTH’s Doctoral student salary agreement
. Read more about
Doctoral studies (PhD) | KTH | Sweden
.
Salary and allowances
– The position is funded through the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) programme. For more information, please see
Doctoral Networks - Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions.
The
Living Allowance
corresponds to approximately
SEK 35,423 per month
and is used to finance the salary paid in accordance with the KTH doctoral salary scale (see the KTH doctoral salary agreement linked above).
In addition, the following allowances are included:
Mobility Allowance:
approximately
SEK 5,017 per month
Family Allowance:
approximately
SEK 4,664 per month
(if the eligibility criteria are fulfilled)
All amounts are stated before tax. The stated amounts are approximate and may vary slightly due to exchange rate fluctuations.
Union representatives
Contact information for
union representatives.

Contact information for

.
To apply for the position
Apply for the position and admission through KTH's recruitment system. It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the advertisement.
Applications must include the following elements:
Copies of diplomas and grades from previous university studies and certificates of fulfilled
language requirements (see above)
. Translations into English or Swedish if the original document is not issued in one of these languages.Copies of originals must be
certified
.
CV including your relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Application letter with a brief description of why you want to pursue research studies, about what your academic interests are and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. (Maximum 2 pages long)
Representative publications or technical reports. For longer documents, please provide a summary (abstract) and a web link to the full text.
Applications must be received at the last closing date at midnight, CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
Other information
Striving towards gender equality, diversity and equal conditions is both a question of quality for KTH and a given part of our values.

ai.summary: Doctoral position in computational and experimental fluid mechanics (non-Newtonian flows) combined with AI and machine learning, within an EU MSCA Doctoral Network (FairCFD). Research integrates high-performance computing, laboratory experiments, and AI pattern recognition to build a digital twin rheometer for characterising complex fluid behaviour.

thematic_fit.rationale: The core research is non-Newtonian fluid mechanics, experimental fluid dynamics, and AI-driven parameter optimisation. No human-centred research, immersive systems, learning science, collaboration, or spatial cognition for human understanding. The 'AI' component is applied to fluid property characterisation, not human-computer interaction or immersive learning. Thematic misalignment is fundamental.

methodological_fit.rationale: Position emphasises computational methods (HPC, numerical simulation), experimental design and execution, and AI/machine learning for pattern recognition in scientific data. The candidate has intermediate experimental design and quantitative research skills from user studies; these methodologies do not transfer well to fluid dynamics experiments or HPC-driven computational modelling. The 'AI' component (pattern extraction, parameter sensitivity) is scientometric/optimisation-focused, not HCI or human learning evaluation. Some overlap in experimental rigour, but core methods diverge significantly.

growth_value.rationale: Exposure to HPC facilities, advanced machine learning integration with physical simulation, and rigorous experimental validation could broaden technical capabilities. However, these skills (HPC, fluid simulation, rheology) are peripheral to the candidate's target identity. The candidate explicitly excludes pure ML algorithm development; this role is heavily algorithm-development-focused (AI-driven rheometer). Growth would be lateral and away from human-centred research.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a strong European technical institution; the doctoral network (FairCFD) is EU MSCA-funded, ensuring 4-year funding stability. However, the FLOW research environment and Complex Fluids group are in mechanical/computational engineering, not HCI. Supervisors (Outi Tammisola, Fredrik Lundell) are fluid mechanics specialists. Completion would not build networks in immersive systems, human-centred XR, or learning science communities. Weak pathway to target institutions (Aalto, TU Delft HCI groups) or target identity.

eligibility_flags: Candidate is currently in MSc thesis stage (not completed). Position requires completed second-cycle degree (Master's) by application or admission deadline. Candidate must complete thesis before formal admission eligibility.

Suitable background described as MSc in engineering, mathematics or physics with focus on fluid mechanics, computational or experimental methods, applied mathematics. Candidate holds MSc in Creative Multimedia. Educational background is not a formal barrier but represents domain shift.

MSCA Doctoral Networks have mobility eligibility rules: candidates must not have resided or conducted main activity in Sweden >12 months in preceding 3 years. Candidate's current location (Malaysia) likely satisfies this, but requires verification.
English proficiency equivalent to B/6 required—likely met, but not explicitly stated in profile.
risks: Fundamental research culture mismatch (fluid mechanics engineering vs. human-centred HCI).
Candidate's target_identity explicitly excludes 'pure-machine-learning-algorithms'; this role heavily emphasises AI/ML-driven optimisation for physical characterisation.
Four-year commitment to a domain orthogonal to target identity (spatial cognition, collaborative immersive systems, learning science).
No supervision or research group connection to HCI, XR, or learning science. Doctoral committee would be fluid mechanics specialists.
Educational background (Creative Multimedia) differs from typical cohort; may experience cultural/methodological friction in a physics/engineering doctoral programme.
Completion would not advance candidacy for target positions at Aalto or HCI-focused groups at TU Delft.
Unilateral domain pivot: completing this PhD would require follow-on postdoc or career restructuring to re-enter immersive systems research.
